notes:
The document stops floating.

Notes now have a **title at the top** — big, editable, and showing the real name
of the thing you're reading. Edit it and the file itself changes: the `title:`
in your frontmatter if you have one, the file name if you don't, with wikilinks
pointing at it updated the way a rename from the explorer already did.

Above it, the pane header gained **back and forward** through the notes you
visited in that pane, and a **breadcrumb** of the file's path. Click a folder in
it and the explorer opens and expands straight to that folder. Each pane keeps
its own trail, and it resets when you quit — closing a tab erases that step
rather than reopening the file behind your back.

At the bottom of the window there's now a **status bar**: word and character
count, how many properties the note has, and how many notes link to it. It
follows whichever pane has focus, and it stays put when focus moves to a
terminal — the numbers go away, the bar doesn't, so nothing above it jumps.

**Line numbers in notes** finally look like they belong. They used to inherit a
pale strip with a border that cut through any theme; now they reuse the same
styling the code editor always had, and they sit in the document's margin
instead of hugging the edge of the pane. Turning them on no longer shifts the
text sideways.

And **text no longer touches the edge** of a narrow pane — the common case when
you split three ways. There's always a margin now, with or without comfortable
margins turned on.
